sentences.text: Streptococcus thermophilus is a lactic acid bacterium of dairy fermentation; strains isolated from goat milk showed efficient lactose fermentation, broad carbohydrate use and high beta-galactosidase activity.

A study of 21,561 individuals across five multinational cohorts found that diet-specific gut microbes partly overlapped with food microbiomes, especially dairy microbes such as Streptococcus thermophilus.

In 330 participants whose faecal microbiome was profiled by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, Streptococcus thermophilus was positively associated with yogurt intake, independently of lactase persistence genotype.
One probiotic strain was reported to inhibit the growth of most bacterial species of the human gut microbiota, with the exception of Bacteroides dorei, which it fed by nutrient cross-feeding.
In that work, co-culture with gut commensals produced bioactive compounds such as folate, and the authors suggested the strain as a potential prophylactic agent for colon cancer.
